subject: health
unitTitle: Feelings, Calm, and Asking for Help
title: Guided practice: where feelings show up in the body
focus: where feelings show up in the body
essentialQuestion: How can I notice what I feel and choose a helpful next step?
materials: paper or cards for a calm-down menu
a card the guardian keeps for trusted-adult contacts
keyPoints: Strong feelings often show up physically: a fast heartbeat, a tight chest, hot cheeks, a churning stomach, or tense shoulders.
These signals are early warnings that can be noticed before a feeling gets big.
Bodies differ, so signals are personal and no one signal is the correct one.
Noticing a signal early gives you more choices about what to do next.
privacySafeScenario: Before reading aloud, Devi's hands shake and her stomach churns. What is her body telling her, and what could she do with that information?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about where feelings show up in the body to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Using the practice situation, say what the safest or healthiest next step is and why.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about where feelings show up in the body.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Calming tools may be movement-based, still, sensory, verbal, or silent, and each learner picks tools their body and setting allow. Any scenario may be answered by pointing, choosing from options, drawing, or speaking.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about where feelings show up in the body under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, agree on one calm-down option that is allowed at home and one that is allowed away from home. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
